contents.html: 1.1 Background
contents.html_ja: 1.1 背景
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: As the U.S. builds its National Information Infrastructure (NII), wide-spread use of encryption will be needed to protect sensitive information. However, wide-spread use of unconstrained encryption makes lawfully-authorized electronic surveillance difficult, if not impossible.
contents.html_ja: 米国が国家情報基盤（NII）を構築するにつれて、機微な情報を保護するために暗号が広く使われる必要が生じます。しかし、制約のない暗号が広く使われると、法的に認められた電子的監視が、不可能ではないにせよ困難になります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: In attempting to balance the need for privacy and the need for lawful surveillance, a Key Escrow Encryption (KEE) technology was developed by the National Security Agency (NSA). The Escrowed Encryption Standard (EES) based on the KEE was issued by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Approved by the Secretary of Commerce<sup>1</sup>, this voluntary standard seeks to satisfy the need for privacy while preserving the ability to perform lawfully authorized wiretaps. This escrowed encryption technology is embodied in an electronic chip containing the SKIPJACK algorithm for encryption of information and the technology for creating a Law Enforcement Access Field (LEAF) for use in many telecommunication applications. Both the SKIPJACK algorithm and the LEAF creation method are classified. The standard is intended to facilitate the acquisition of devices that implement KEE technologies by Federal government agencies. Its use is not mandated for Federal agencies, the private sector, or other levels of government.
contents.html_ja: プライバシーの必要性と合法的な監視の必要性の均衡を図るため、国家安全保障局（NSA）が鍵預託暗号（KEE）の技術を開発しました。KEE に基づく鍵預託暗号化標準（EES）は、国立標準技術研究所（NIST）が発行しました。この標準は商務長官が承認したもの<sup>1</sup>で、任意の標準であり、合法的に認められた盗聴を行う能力を保ちつつ、プライバシーの必要性を満たすことを目指しています。この預託暗号の技術は、情報を暗号化する SKIPJACK アルゴリズムと、多くの電気通信アプリケーションで使用する法執行機関アクセスフィールド（LEAF）を作成する技術を収めた電子チップに実装されています。SKIPJACK アルゴリズムと LEAF の作成方法は、いずれも機密扱いです。この標準は、連邦政府機関による KEE 技術を実装した装置の調達を容易にすることを意図しています。連邦機関、民間部門、その他の政府レベルに対して、その使用は義務付けられていません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: In using the Escrowed Encryption Standard, communications are encrypted by the SKIPJACK algorithm using a session key agreed upon by the participating entities. The appended LEAF field, which contains among other things the session key (encrypted using the device unique key), is itself encrypted with an 80-bit family key. The only known way of recovering the session key is to first recover the two 80-bit components of the device unique key. Each of these components is “escrowed” (i.e., filed) in encrypted form with one of two escrow agents. The two escrow agents act under strict procedures that will ensure security of the key components and govern their release. Surveillance requires acquisition of both escrowed key components, through a predefined process.
contents.html_ja: 鍵預託暗号化標準を使用する場合、通信は、参加するエンティティが合意したセッション鍵を用いて SKIPJACK アルゴリズムにより暗号化されます。付加される LEAF フィールドには、とりわけセッション鍵（装置固有鍵で暗号化されたもの）が含まれ、LEAF フィールド自体は 80 ビットのファミリー鍵で暗号化されます。セッション鍵を回復する既知の方法は、まず装置固有鍵の 2 つの 80 ビット構成要素を回復する方法だけです。これらの構成要素はそれぞれ、暗号化された形で 2 つの預託機関のそれぞれに「預託」（すなわち保管）されます。2 つの預託機関は、鍵の構成要素の安全性を保証し、その開示を管理する厳格な手続に従って行動します。監視を行うには、あらかじめ定められた手続を通じて、預託された 2 つの鍵の構成要素の両方を入手する必要があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Based on the desire to use existing expertise in the private sector and motivated partially by requirements of non-government entities, NIST has invited interested industry and academic partners to join a cooperative research consortium for developing the next generation of encryption technology that contains integrated cryptographic key escrowing techniques. In addition, an informal industry/government working group was established to explore the possibilities of software implementation of key escrowing. Finally, representatives from key U.S. industries were invited to participate in this workshop in order to initiate a dialogue on the issues of escrowing encryption keys. This partnership with the private sector is necessary to arrive at a mutually acceptable solution that will balance the need for privacy, the need for lawful electronic surveillance, and the needs of industry, both as users and vendors.
contents.html_ja: NIST は、民間部門の既存の専門知識を活用したいという考えと、非政府エンティティの要件にも一部動機づけられて、関心のある産業界および学界のパートナーに対し、暗号鍵の預託技術を統合した次世代の暗号技術を開発する共同研究コンソーシアムへの参加を呼びかけました。さらに、鍵預託のソフトウェア実装の可能性を探るため、産業界と政府の非公式の作業部会が設けられました。最後に、暗号鍵の預託に関する問題について対話を始めるため、米国の主要産業の代表者が、このワークショップに参加するよう招かれました。このような民間部門との連携は、プライバシーの必要性、合法的な電子的監視の必要性、そして利用者としても供給者としても産業界のニーズの均衡をとる、相互に受け入れ可能な解決策に至るために必要です。

contents.html: 2.1 Session 1: Opening Session
contents.html_ja: 2.1 セッション 1: 開会セッション

contents.html: Senior government officials discussed the objectives of the workshop in light of the key escrow encryption initiative announced in April, 1993. This initiative seeks to provide good encryption-based security to a number of information processing environments while preserving the lawful interests of law enforcement and national security. The Escrowed Encryption Standard (EES), announced as Federal Information Processing Standard 185 on February 4, 1994, resulted from this initiative. In addition, the “CLIPPER” escrowed encryption device was designed and built under this initiative. Finally, a Key Escrow System is being designed and implemented to store the escrowed keys securely and make them available to authorized entities for legally authorized electronic surveillance.
contents.html_ja: 政府の高官が、1993 年 4 月に発表された鍵預託暗号の構想を踏まえて、ワークショップの目的を論じました。この構想は、法執行と国家安全保障という正当な利益を保ちつつ、多くの情報処理環境に暗号に基づく優れたセキュリティを提供することを目指しています。1994 年 2 月 4 日に連邦情報処理標準 185 として発表された鍵預託暗号化標準（EES）は、この構想から生まれました。さらに、この構想の下で、“CLIPPER” 預託暗号装置が設計・製造されました。最後に、預託された鍵を安全に保管し、法的に認められた電子的監視のために、権限のあるエンティティが利用できるようにする鍵預託システムが、設計・実装されつつあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Raymond G. Kammer, Deputy Director of NIST, and F. Lynn McNulty, Associate Director for Computer Security at NIST, provided the welcoming and introductory remarks. (Mr. McNulty also served as moderator for the workshop.) Mssrs. Kammer and McNulty stated that the objective of the workshop was to engage the private sector in dialogue on the issues of key escrow encryption.
contents.html_ja: NIST の Deputy Director である Raymond G. Kammer と、NIST のコンピューターセキュリティ担当の Associate Director である F. Lynn McNulty が、歓迎の辞と冒頭の挨拶を述べました。（McNulty 氏はワークショップの司会も務めました。）Kammer 氏と McNulty 氏は、ワークショップの目的は、鍵預託暗号の問題について民間部門との対話に取り組むことだと述べました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Lionel “Skip” Johns, Associate Director of Technology, Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President, stated that the National Security Council has the responsibility of coordinating security policy in the Executive Branch of the U.S. Government. Intelligence remains a critical activity of national interest and the U.S. must be able to detect and act in a timely manner on real threats of terrorism, crime, and danger to the national security. OSTP seeks to engage in dialogue with U.S. industry so that effective intelligence collection can be conducted with a minimal threat to privacy. He stated that acceptable solutions may be hard to find and, unfortunately, a final solution may be suboptimal.
contents.html_ja: 大統領府の科学技術政策局（OSTP）で技術担当の Associate Director を務める Lionel “Skip” Johns 氏は、国家安全保障会議が、米国政府の行政部門における安全保障政策の調整に責任を負っていると述べました。情報活動は引き続き国益にとって重要な活動であり、米国は、テロ、犯罪、国家安全保障への危険という現実の脅威を探知し、時宜を得て対処できなければならないとしました。OSTP は、プライバシーへの脅威を最小限にとどめながら効果的な情報収集を行えるよう、米国の産業界との対話に取り組むことを目指しています。同氏は、受け入れ可能な解決策を見つけるのは難しい場合があり、残念ながら、最終的な解決策が最適ではないものになる可能性もあると述べました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: William Crowell, Deputy Director of the National Security Agency, pointed out the need to ensure that a balance is achieved among four equities: privacy, public safety, ability to market new products, and national security. Three options, when implementing cryptography, are possible: flawed cryptography, strong cryptography with contents unreadable by all, and key escrowing. The latter seemed to have the most viability for achieving balance among the four equities. CLIPPER is a first (interim) solution – there is a need to look at more software intensive solutions. Edward Hart, Deputy Director for Information Systems Security, NSA, reiterated NSA’s desire for openness, collegiality, and desire to work with U.S. industry in seeking mutually acceptable solutions.
contents.html_ja: 国家安全保障局の Deputy Director である William Crowell 氏は、プライバシー、公共の安全、新製品を市場に出す能力、国家安全保障という 4 つの利益の間で均衡を確保する必要があると指摘しました。暗号を実装する際に取りうる選択肢は、欠陥のある暗号、内容が誰にも読めない強力な暗号、鍵預託の 3 つです。最後の鍵預託が、4 つの利益の均衡をとるうえで最も実現性が高いように見えました。CLIPPER は最初の（暫定的な）解決策であり、よりソフトウェア中心の解決策を検討する必要があるとしました。NSA の Deputy Director for Information Systems Security である Edward Hart 氏は、NSA が開かれた姿勢と協調性を望んでおり、相互に受け入れ可能な解決策を探る上で米国の産業界と協力したいと考えていることを改めて述べました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Industry participants, in an open discussion, raised the following issues/questions/concerns:
contents.html_ja: 産業界の参加者は、自由討議の中で、次の問題・疑問・懸念を提起しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Currently the delay in obtaining licenses to export products prevents U.S. industry from being internationally competitive.
contents.html_ja: 現在、製品の輸出許可の取得に遅れが生じており、そのために米国の産業界が国際的な競争力を持てずにいます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: The uncertainty over whether a license will be granted discourages even applying for a license. There needs to be more information as to what applications have been made and their disposition. A counter-point is the need for nondisclosure of export license applications that might compromise the economic interests of the applicants or compromise the interests of national security.
contents.html_ja: 許可が下りるかどうかが不確実なため、申請すること自体が敬遠されています。どのような申請が行われ、どう処理されたかについて、より多くの情報が必要です。これに対する反論として、申請者の経済的利益を損なうおそれのある、あるいは国家安全保障上の利益を損なうおそれのある輸出許可申請について、非公開にする必要があるという点が挙げられました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Given the four equities, how are we planning for change? It is important that we not be constrained in meeting future needs.
contents.html_ja: 4 つの利益を前提とした場合、変化にどう備えるのか。将来のニーズに応える上で制約を受けないことが重要です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: If the CLIPPER Chip is only an interim solution, why not wait for a final solution? The response was that key escrowing is an integral part of current cryptography policy and will be so through all stages of evolution.
contents.html_ja: CLIPPER Chip が暫定的な解決策にすぎないのなら、なぜ最終的な解決策を待たないのか。これに対し、鍵預託は現行の暗号政策の不可欠な一部であり、今後の進展のどの段階でもそうあり続けるとの回答がありました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Foreign countries have proprietary encryption algorithms that they want to put into chips. What restrictions apply on manufacturing the chips in the U.S.? Is an open dialogue with NSA possible on this? NSA stated that they supported the capitalistic free enterprise system and invited dialogue with industry on the issues as how the current regulating processes might be changed.
contents.html_ja: 外国には、チップに組み込みたい独自の暗号アルゴリズムがあります。米国内でそのチップを製造することには、どのような制限が適用されるのか。この点について NSA と率直に対話することは可能か。NSA は、資本主義的な自由企業体制を支持していると述べ、現行の規制の手続をどのように変更しうるかという問題について、産業界との対話を歓迎しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: It was noted that security of information is an international issue and is not a new issue.
contents.html_ja: 情報のセキュリティは国際的な問題であり、新しい問題ではないという指摘がありました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: There is a need for NSA to have a dialogue with industry and academia to define new processes to meet the requirements of global information security. The primary concern for industry is satisfying the security needs of their commercial customers. The response was that a process has to be developed, amenable to all interests.
contents.html_ja: NSA は、地球規模の情報セキュリティの要件を満たす新しい手続を定義するため、産業界および学界と対話する必要があります。産業界にとっての主な関心事は、商用の顧客のセキュリティ上のニーズを満たすことです。これに対し、あらゆる利害関係者が受け入れられる手続を作る必要があるとの回答がありました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Concern was expressed for the feeling that, when industry raises an export problem with NSA, industry representatives have their integrity questioned. NSA needs to be more responsive and less critical of intent.
contents.html_ja: 産業界が輸出の問題を NSA に提起すると、産業界の代表者が自分たちの誠実さを疑われているように感じるという懸念が示されました。NSA は、より迅速に対応し、意図をむやみに批判しないようにする必要があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Concern was expressed that there may not be a satisfactory solution to balance the four equities.
contents.html_ja: 4 つの利益の均衡をとる満足のいく解決策がない可能性があるという懸念が示されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: With regard to the import/export of cryptography, individuals in foreign countries want to use their own algorithms – they do not trust ours. At present, we are unable to export the technology they want. The response was for industry to provide the technology to NSA for their approval for export.
contents.html_ja: 暗号の輸入・輸出に関して、外国の個人は自国のアルゴリズムを使いたがっています。米国のものは信用されていません。現時点では、彼らが望む技術を輸出することはできません。これに対し、産業界がその技術を NSA に提供し、輸出の承認を求めるべきだとの回答がありました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: It was further noted that foreign countries sell DES products to the U.S. but the U.S. cannot sell U.S. products containing DES to them. For example, DES can be purchased in such places as Moscow, Singapore, and Stockholm. Kerberos, with any encryption technique, is available outside the U.S. but U.S. industry is not allowed to export it. U.S. companies are unable to compete for the global market for cryptographic devices and, from the standpoint of technology and economics, are falling behind (or losing ground to) other nations.

contents.html: View graphs were shown describing how the KEE system is designed to work: manufacturing of the chip, programming of the the chip, key escrowing with two independent government agents (NIST, Department of Treasury), obtaining court authorization for a wire tap and the corresponding release of keys, and decryption of communications.
contents.html_ja: KEE システムがどのように動作するよう設計されているかを説明するビューグラフが示されました。内容は、チップの製造、チップのプログラミング、2 つの独立した政府機関（NIST、財務省）による鍵預託、盗聴の裁判所による許可の取得とそれに伴う鍵の開示、通信の復号です。

contents.html: Four phases of key escrowing have been defined. The first phase, consisting of developing a prototype system, has been completed. The first programming of a chip took place in October, 1993 and by March, 1994, the keys for 17,000 CLIPPER chips had been escrowed. At present, no key components have been released. Phases 2-4 are designed to move from the prototype system to a target production system. The target system will include automated procedures for handling and storing escrow components, a decryption processor, a simple key component extraction system, an escrow agent workstation, and a transition to life cycle support. A number of evaluations are planned during phases 2-4. Recent efforts have included preparing for key escrowing for CAPSTONE. Also, the Vice-President has asked for a review of other possible escrow agents.
contents.html_ja: 鍵預託システムには 4 つのフェーズが定められています。試作システムの開発から成る第 1 フェーズは完了しています。チップの最初のプログラミングは 1993 年 10 月に行われ、1994 年 3 月までに 17,000 個の CLIPPER チップの鍵が預託されました。現時点では、鍵の構成要素は一つも開示されていません。フェーズ 2〜4 は、試作システムから目標とする本番システムへ移行するよう設計されています。目標システムには、預託された構成要素を取り扱い保管するための自動化された手続、復号プロセッサー、簡素な鍵構成要素の抽出システム、預託機関のワークステーション、ライフサイクル支援への移行が含まれます。フェーズ 2〜4 では、いくつかの評価が計画されています。最近の取り組みには、CAPSTONE の鍵預託の準備が含まれます。また、副大統領は、ほかに預託機関となりうる機関の検討を求めました。

contents.html: Cellular phone conversations are clear at the switch and therefore do not need key escrow to allow for law enforcement. Most customers expect security at no additional cost. Encryption algorithms should be available to all manufacturers worldwide. Manufacturers need to be able to implement the encryption algorithms in their own processes; the method for doing the key escrow needs to be simplified; standards have to be defined. The current direction in using smart cards for authentication do not match concepts for key escrowing.

contents.html: 2.3.1 A Software Key Escrow Approach, Stephen T. Walker (Member of Working Group) and David M. Balenson, Trusted Information Systems, Inc.

contents.html_ja: 非政府の 4 名（Cole、Denning、Upton、Walker）と政府機関の 2 名（Arney、Branstad）からなる作業部会が、ソフトウェアで鍵預託暗号を行う方法を探ってきました。その動機は、法執行の目的を達成する、広く受け入れられる低コストのシステムを開発することです。このシステムも、CLIPPER/CAPSTONE と同様、決意の固いソフトウェアハッカーに破られる可能性があります。
contents.html: A working group consisting of four non-government individuals (Cole, Denning, Upton, Walker) and two government agency individuals (Arney, Branstad) have been exploring ways to perform key escrow encryption in software. The motivation is to develop a broadly acceptable, low-cost system that achieves the objectives of law enforcement. It does not solve problems that CLIPPER/CAPSTONE do not solve as both can be defeated by a determined software hacker.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。見出しと本文を分けた。行末で分かれた語を直した。

contents.html: Many aspects of the design and usage are similar to the specifications in the EES. Rather than secret key cryptography, the proposed model uses public key cryptography and will work with any public key algorithm although software implementations cannot keep the algorithm secret. It will work with PCM cards. Components of a private key are escrowed with two independent escrow agents. Each instance of the software is a shrink-wrapped package, with a unique ID assigned to it either at the time of creation or the time of first invocation, and with embedded cryptographic checksums to guard against code modification. This ID is provided in a LEAF which is created by the software when invoked. The method of escrowing keys and their authorized retrieval by law enforcement agencies was outlined.
contents.html_ja: 設計と利用の多くの面は、EES の仕様に似ています。共通鍵暗号ではなく、この提案のモデルは公開鍵暗号を使用し、ソフトウェアによる実装ではアルゴリズムを秘密にできないものの、どの公開鍵アルゴリズムとも動作します。PCM カードでも動作します。秘密鍵の構成要素は、2 つの独立した預託機関に預託されます。ソフトウェアの個々のインスタンスは、シュリンクラップ形式のパッケージで、作成時または最初の起動時に固有の ID が割り当てられ、コードの改変に備える暗号チェックサムが埋め込まれます。この ID は、ソフトウェアが起動されたときに作成する LEAF に含まれます。鍵を預託する方法と、法執行機関が権限に基づいて鍵を取得する方法が概説されました。

contents.html: Key escrowing is fundamentally a good idea, but something more is required. The need for key escrowing may arise in multiple contexts: state vs. company (may need keys escrowed inside), communications vs. stored data (will be retrieved later), simple private call (friend) vs. recorded private call (stock broker), national vs. international context, etc. What is needed is multi-purpose key escrowing.
contents.html_ja: 鍵預託は基本的に良い考え方ですが、それ以上のものが必要です。鍵預託の必要性は、国家と企業（内部で鍵を預託する必要がある場合があります）、通信と保存データ（後で取り出されるもの）、単純な私的通話（友人との通話）と記録される私的通話（株式仲買人との通話）など、複数の文脈で生じる場合があります。必要なのは、複数の目的に使える鍵預託です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: The proposal is for “Fair Public Key Cryptography (PKC)” as an alternative to the CLIPPER Chip. Fair PKC is distributed, flexible, open, economical, and complete, whereas the CLIPPER Chip is centralized, rigid, hidden, expensive, and partial. Private key cryptosystems have limited use because of the need for key management; on the other hand, in public key cryptosystems, through the use of public directories, it is easy to talk to someone you have never met. In the CLIPPER chip, the focus of attention has been on the issues of escrowing, but communicating entities still need to establish a session key.
contents.html_ja: この提案は、CLIPPER Chip の代替案として「Fair Public Key Cryptography（PKC）」を示すものです。CLIPPER Chip が中央集権的、硬直的、非公開、高価で部分的であるのに対し、Fair PKC は分散型、柔軟、公開、経済的で完全です。共通鍵暗号方式は、鍵管理が必要なため用途が限られます。一方、公開鍵暗号方式では、公開ディレクトリを使って、会ったことのない相手とも容易に通信できます。CLIPPER Chip では、注意が預託の問題に向けられてきましたが、通信するエンティティは、依然としてセッション鍵を確立する必要があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: From a law enforcement perspective, the idea of combining public key cryptosystems with private key cryptosystems is not a good one. Individuals can use the public system to exchange the private key K and then can use a standard method (e.g., DES) to encrypt. The key is not available to law enforcement for an authorized wiretap. Furthermore, the encryption can be made reasonably strong, e.g., \(E_{K_1}(D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(\mathit{message})))\).
contents.html_ja: 法執行の観点では、公開鍵暗号方式と共通鍵暗号方式を組み合わせる考え方は好ましくありません。個人は、公開方式で共通鍵 K を交換し、その後、標準的な方法（DES など）で暗号化できます。この鍵は、権限に基づく盗聴のために法執行機関が利用することはできません。さらに、暗号化は、たとえば \(E_{K_1}(D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(\mathit{message})))\) のように、十分に強くすることができます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像（scale 5 の部分描画）と語・記号ごとに照合した。3 段落が 1 ブロックに入っていたので分け、崩れた数式（添字・平方根・べき）を LaTeX で書き直した。続きの断片 pdf-p0018-b0010〜b0012 を retire した。原本の「where a is less b」はそのまま残した。
contents.translation_resolve_note: “private key cryptosystems” はこの文脈では共通鍵方式で、K は DES 用の共通鍵。「共通鍵」が正しい。

contents.html_ja: Fair PKC は次のように動作します。まず、公開鍵 \(PK\) と秘密鍵 \(SK\) のペアを決めます。秘密鍵は 2 つの構成要素 \(SK_1\) と \(SK_2\) に分割され、第 1 の構成要素は受託者 \(T_1\) に、第 2 の構成要素は \(T_2\) に預託されます。\(T_1\) と \(T_2\) はそれぞれ、もう一方の構成要素を実際に知らなくても、自分が \(SK\) の正当な構成要素を持っていることを証明できます。公開鍵はセンターに登録され、承認されます（すなわち、配布に利用できるようになります）。法執行機関は、受託者から秘密鍵の構成要素を入手する必要があります。
contents.html: Fair PKC works in the following way. First, determine a public key \(PK\), secret key \(SK\) pair. The secret key is divided into two components \(SK_1\) and \(SK_2\), the first of which is escrowed with trustee \(T_1\) and the second escrowed with \(T_2\). Each of \(T_1\) and \(T_2\) can certify that they have a legitimate component of \(SK\) without actually knowing the other component. The public key is filed with a center and approved (i.e., made available for distribution). Law enforcement requires acquisition of the secret key components from the trustees.

contents.html_ja: Fair PKC がどのように動作するかを示す類推を次に示します。公開鍵を \(X\)、秘密鍵を \(\sqrt{X}\) とし、平方根はある数 n を法として求めるものとします。秘密鍵を見つける困難さは、平方根を見つける困難さ（因数分解と同程度に困難です）に基づいています。利用者は、\(\sqrt{a}\) と \(\sqrt{b}\) と定義される 2 つの数を選び、それらが \(\mathrm{SK}_1\) と \(\mathrm{SK}_2\) となります。利用者は、\(\mathrm{a} = (\sqrt{a})^2\) と \(\mathrm{b} = (\sqrt{b})^2\) を作り、公開鍵 \(X = a * b\)、秘密鍵 \(\sqrt{X} = \sqrt{a} * \sqrt{b}\) を作ります。受託者 \(T_1\) には \((X, a, b, \sqrt{a})\) が、\(T_2\) には \((X, a, b, \sqrt{b})\) が渡されます。ここで \(a\) は \(b\) より小さいものとします。\(T_1\) は \(X = a * b\) と \((\sqrt{a})^2 = a\) を確認でき、同様に \(T_2\) も、自分が正当な秘密鍵の構成要素を持っていることを証明できます。しかし、どちらも相手の受託者が保持する構成要素を特定することはできません。法執行機関は、権限があれば、受託者から構成要素を入手して、秘密鍵 \(\sqrt{X}\) を作ることができます。
contents.html: Here is an analogy of how Fair PKC might work. Suppose the public key is \(X\) and the private key is \(\sqrt{X}\), where the square root is performed modulo some number n. The difficulty of finding the secret key is based on the difficulty of finding the square root (which is as hard as factoring). The user selects two numbers which are defined to be \(\sqrt{a}\) and \(\sqrt{b}\) and serve as \(\mathrm{SK}_1\) and \(\mathrm{SK}_2\). The user forms \(\mathrm{a} = (\sqrt{a})^2\) and \(\mathrm{b} = (\sqrt{b})^2\),the public key \(X = a * b\), and the secret key \(\sqrt{X} = \sqrt{a} * \sqrt{b}\). Trustee \(T_1\) is given \((X, a, b, \sqrt{a})\) and \(T_2\) is given \((X, a, b, \sqrt{b})\) where \(a\) is less \(b\). \(T_1\) can check \(X = a * b\) and \((\sqrt{a})^2 = a\) and similarly \(T_2\) can certify that it has a component of a legitimate secret key. But each is unable to determine the component held by the other trustee. A law enforcement agency, if authorized, can obtain the components from the trustees and form the private key \(\sqrt{X}\).

contents.html: The espoused encryption model would maintain privacy at the “file level”. It is then no longer necessary to secure the channel in order to maintain privacy of communicated information. Individuals would be in charge of encrypting their own files and would maintain their own own keys in a manner regulated by legislation. In the event of a suspected crime or a suspected threat to national security, the government can obtain a court order and subpoena the keys. The theory is that individuals who, to avoid prosecution, destroy their keys would also destroy their access to the information. To operate in the international arena, there would be a suite of multiple independent software algorithms that would satisfy the international community and the U.S. government. TECSEC has an application program VEIL that supports these ideas.
contents.html_ja: 提唱された暗号モデルは、「ファイルレベル」でプライバシーを維持します。そのため、通信される情報のプライバシーを維持するために通信路を保護する必要はなくなります。個人は自分のファイルの暗号化を自ら担い、法律で規制される方法で自分の鍵を自ら保持することになります。犯罪の疑いや国家安全保障への脅威の疑いがある場合、政府は裁判所の命令を得て、召喚状により鍵の提出を求めることができます。訴追を逃れるために鍵を破棄する個人は、その情報にアクセスする手段も失うことになる、という考え方です。国際的な場で運用するため、国際社会と米国政府の双方を満たす、独立した複数のソフトウェアアルゴリズムの一式を用意します。TECSEC は、これらの考え方を支援するアプリケーションプログラム VEIL を持っています。

contents.html: Use of a key escrowed encryption device in a security application requires a high level of system integrity to assure that all security relevant events are performed correctly. Utilization of a key escrowed encryption device (e.g. CAPSTONE) in a more complex information processing application such as distributed electronic commerce requires many functions of the computer system to have high integrity, both to assure that the data is properly protected and also that the the LEAF field is transmitted and received properly. Integrity requirements for software encryption and operating system controlled execution were the subject of this session.
contents.html_ja: 鍵預託暗号装置をセキュリティアプリケーションで使用するには、セキュリティに関連するすべてのイベントが正しく実行されることを保証するために、高いレベルのシステム完全性が必要です。鍵預託暗号装置（たとえば CAPSTONE）を、分散型電子商取引のようなより複雑な情報処理アプリケーションで利用するには、データが適切に保護されることと、LEAF フィールドが適切に送受信されることの両方を保証するため、コンピューターシステムの多くの機能に高い完全性が必要です。ソフトウェア暗号とオペレーティングシステムが制御する実行に関する完全性要件が、このセッションの主題でした。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Jim Dray presented a model for an escrowed encryption device. Important points to be noted are the need for an interface between the cryptographic device and the general purpose system and the need to communicate through untrusted layers of software. The threat scenarios include all communication pairs: rogue system/rogue system, rogue system/legitimate system, legitimate system/legitimate system. The high-level implications are that one needs to prevent use of an EES device that circumvents the LEAF; it would be ideal to design cryptographic modules to withstand attacks in an untrusted environment; and the LEAF imposes additional requirements.
contents.html_ja: Jim Dray は、預託暗号装置のモデルを示しました。注目すべき重要な点は、暗号装置と汎用システムの間にインターフェースが必要なこと、および信頼できないソフトウェア層を通して通信する必要があることです。脅威シナリオには、すべての通信の組み合わせが含まれます。すなわち、不正なシステムどうし、不正なシステムと正規のシステム、正規のシステムどうしです。大局的な含意は、LEAF を回避する EES 装置の使用を防ぐ必要があること、暗号モジュールは信頼できない環境での攻撃に耐えるよう設計するのが理想的であること、そして LEAF が追加の要件を課すことです。

contents.html: A system security paradigm was outlined for evaluating KEE alternatives. It is important to remind oneself about the user/customer needs for integrity, confidentiality, and availability. Design requirements are needed to approach the problem. The development of a solution is evolutionary because initial perspectives may be short-sighted and because threats may change. Evaluation/verification is required. The design requirements need to consider both the higher algorithm/protocol level and also the implementation level in hardware and software. Good software engineering is a starting point to the effective protection of embedded software cryptography.
contents.html_ja: KEE の代替案を評価するためのシステムセキュリティの枠組みが、概略として示されました。完全性、機密性、可用性に対する利用者・顧客のニーズを改めて心に留めておくことが重要です。この問題に取り組むには、設計要件が必要です。解決策の開発は段階的に進みます。当初の見方は近視眼的であるかもしれず、脅威も変化しうるためです。評価・検証が必要です。設計要件では、上位のアルゴリズム・プロトコルのレベルと、ハードウェアおよびソフトウェアでの実装レベルの両方を考慮する必要があります。優れたソフトウェア工学は、組み込みソフトウェア暗号を効果的に保護するための出発点です。

contents.html_ja: 2.5.2 ソフトウェア完全性のシステム要件、Stephen W. Walker、社長、Trusted Information Systems, Inc.

contents.html: Software integrity is needed unless the entire computing system is packaged in a box that is highly resistant to reverse engineering. Two years ago, TIS was asked by ARPA to develop technical means for controlling high-performance workstations so that the government might be willing to allow their export to such countries as China and Russia for use in “approved” applications. In this project (called the ARPA Safeguards Project), a technology base was identified for controlling the execution of the operating system so that it would only run on a given machine; its modification would be resisted by storing it on some kind of read-only medium; and it would be packaged in a tamper-resistant box (which included methods of tamper detection and audit reporting to the U.S.).
contents.html_ja: コンピューティングシステム全体をリバースエンジニアリングに強い耐性を持つ箱に収めるのでない限り、ソフトウェアの完全性が必要です。2年前、TIS は ARPA から、高性能ワークステーションを制御する技術的手段を開発するよう依頼されました。政府が、中国やロシアなどの国への輸出を「承認された」用途に限って認められるようにするためです。このプロジェクト（ARPA Safeguards Project と呼ばれます）では、オペレーティングシステムの実行を特定の機械でしか行えないよう制御し、何らかの読み取り専用媒体に格納して変更を防ぎ、耐タンパー性のある箱（改ざん検知と米国への監査報告の方法を含む）に収めるための技術基盤が特定されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: The insight gained in developing these controlled execution procedures is directly applicable to any software system where the integrity of the software must be preserved. It can be used for controlled execution of an operating system. The programs are stored on ROM and require a digital signature as authorization to effect an update (therefore also resistant to viruses).
contents.html_ja: これらの制御された実行の手続の開発で得られた知見は、ソフトウェアの完全性を維持しなければならないあらゆるソフトウェアシステムに直接適用できます。オペレーティングシステムの制御された実行に利用できます。プログラムは ROM に格納され、更新を行うための認可としてディジタル署名が必要です（そのため、ウイルスにも耐性があります）。

contents.html_ja: Jim Schindler と Keith Klemba が、Hewlett-Packard 社の取り組みを説明しました。HP は、何が必要かを判断するため、国内外の顧客層を調べました。その結果の意見は、セキュリティ機能はハードウェアとソフトウェアの両方で必要であること、暗号技術がアプリケーションとインターフェースをとる方法を安定させる必要があること、そしてさまざまな政府に共通する暗号政策の枠組みが必要であることでした。
contents.html: Jim Schindler and Keith Klemba described the work of Hewlett-Packard Company. HP had looked at its domestic/foreign customer base to determine what was needed. The sentiments were that security functions were needed in both hardware and software; there was a need to stabilize the manner in which the crypto technology interfaces with applications; and a common cryptographic policy framework was needed for various governments.

contents.html: HP has designed a “national flag” card (NFC), about the size of a postage stamp, that would enforce the cryptographic policy of a nation. The NFC would fit into a drawer in a cryptographic unit (CU) which is designed to provide cryptographic services (under the strict control of the NFC). The NFC is removable, interchangeable, and expirable. The CU would be designed for performance and protection with customization for a given host system. The initial discussions for the CU have centered around a PCMCIA hardware format. The CU features protection of the keys and algorithms and would likely have to be certified.
contents.html_ja: HP は、切手ほどの大きさの「国旗」カード（NFC）を設計しました。これは、国の暗号政策を強制するものです。NFC は、暗号サービスを（NFC の厳格な管理下で）提供するよう設計された暗号ユニット（CU）の引き出しに収まります。NFC は取り外し可能で、交換可能であり、有効期限を設定できます。CU は性能と保護を考慮して設計され、特定のホストシステム向けにカスタマイズされます。CU についての当初の議論では、PCMCIA のハードウェア形式が中心となっていました。CU は鍵とアルゴリズムを保護し、おそらく認証を受ける必要があります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: The host system is some hardware component that delivers information technology service to the user (e.g., personal computer or laptop, workstation, network server, mainframe, network printer, personal digital assistant). contents.html: Dorothy Denning talked about her personal research on international aspects of key escrowing. Four general requirements were identified for an international key escrow system: encryption products that provide secure communications, a key escrow system for authorized government access, international communications, and use of encryption products outside of the country that holds the key.
contents.html_ja: Dorothy Denning は、鍵預託の国際的側面に関する自身の研究について話しました。国際的な鍵預託システムの一般的な要件として、4 つが挙げられました。安全な通信を提供する暗号製品、権限に基づく政府のアクセスのための鍵預託システム、国際通信、そして鍵を保持する国の外での暗号製品の使用です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: The general properties of escrowed encryption are: strong security, authorized government access, hardware or software implementations, classified or unclassified algorithms, multiple standards and gateways, and private sector key escrow - separate or integrated.
contents.html_ja: 預託暗号の一般的な特性は、強力なセキュリティ、権限に基づく政府のアクセス、ハードウェアまたはソフトウェアでの実装、機密扱いまたは機密扱いでないアルゴリズム、複数の標準とゲートウェイ、および民間部門の鍵預託（別個のものまたは統合されたもの）です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: National control is needed over the import/export/use of products and over who holds the keys. International and bilateral agreements are needed to assist in criminal investigations, sharing of technologies, and constraints on the sale and use of products. Several national policy options for export and for internal use of products were presented. Law enforcement scenarios were enumerated, e.g., country A wishes to investigate subject X from country B and country C holds the encryption key.
contents.html_ja: 製品の輸入・輸出・使用と、誰が鍵を保持するかについて、国の管理が必要です。犯罪捜査の支援、技術の共有、製品の販売と使用に対する制約のために、国際協定や二国間協定が必要です。製品の輸出と国内での使用に関するいくつかの国家政策の選択肢が示されました。法執行のシナリオが列挙されました。たとえば、A国がB国の対象者Xを捜査しようとしており、C国が暗号鍵を保持している場合です。

contents.html: 3.2 Closing Comments from Industry Participants

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Q1. Other approaches to key escrowing have been presented. Does the charter for the industry/government working group allow for discussion of alternatives that might be more internationally acceptable?
contents.html_ja: Q1. 鍵預託の他の手法が示されました。産業界・政府の作業部会の憲章は、国際的により受け入れられうる代替案の議論を認めていますか。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: That would be allowed – re-analysis is acceptable.
contents.html_ja: それは認められます。再分析は受け入れ可能です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Q2. The general concerns are as follows. The government started with the CLIPPER chip technology as the solution. Industry got it restricted for use only in voice, FAX, and low-speed data communications. But it is being pushed by the government into higher bandwidth communications. All of this is happening without addressing such things as software solutions and international problems.
contents.html_ja: Q2. 一般的な懸念は次のとおりです。政府は、CLIPPER チップの技術を解決策として出発しました。産業界は、その使用を音声、FAX、低速データ通信に限定させました。しかし政府は、より広帯域の通信へとそれを押し進めています。これらはすべて、ソフトウェアによる解決策や国際的な問題などに取り組まないまま進んでいます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。p.26 に続く Q2 の段落をまとめた（脚注 3 の後半と混ざっていた続きのブロックから本文だけを取った）。

contents.html: <sup>3</sup> Lynn McNulty, Associate Director for Computer Security, NIST, Technology Building, Room B-154, Gaithersburg, MD 20899 (Tel: 301-975-3240, Fax: 301-948-1784, email: mcnulty@ecf.ncsl.nist.gov).
contents.html_ja: <sup>3</sup> Lynn McNulty, Associate Director for Computer Security, NIST, Technology Building, Room B-154, Gaithersburg, MD 20899 (Tel: 301-975-3240, Fax: 301-948-1784, email: mcnulty@ecf.ncsl.nist.gov).
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。脚注 3 の全文を 1 ブロックにまとめた（続きは pdf-p0025-b0019、b0020 に分かれていた）。OCR の誤り（F«ix）を直した。

contents.html: The administration will feel that key escrowing is desirable for the development of the NII. The current solutions may not be final, but the government feels that the key escrowing technology is definitely the way to go.
contents.html_ja: 政府は、鍵預託が NII の発展にとって望ましいと考えるでしょう。現在の解決策は最終的なものではないかもしれませんが、政府は、鍵預託の技術が間違いなく進むべき道だと考えています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Q3. In Tessera, there are a number of unstated issues for the IRS, law enforcement, etc. The goal is simply to expand. Industry does not in general disagree – they would like to “sell” it.
contents.html_ja: Q3. Tessera には、IRS や法執行機関などにとって、明示されていない問題が数多くあります。目標は、単に拡大することです。産業界は、一般に異議はなく、それを「売りたい」と考えています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Q4. Who is actually making the decision to push the technologies of Tessera and key escrow?
contents.html_ja: Q4. Tessera や鍵預託の技術を推し進める決定を実際に下しているのは誰か。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: No decision has been made on the applicability of Tessera. The use of the key escrow is voluntary.
contents.html_ja: Tessera の適用可能性についての決定は下されていません。鍵預託の使用は任意です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。OCR の誤りを直した。

contents.html: Q5. How about the secrecy of SKIPJACK?
contents.html_ja: Q5. SKIPJACK の秘密性はどうなるのか。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: It has been reviewed by NSA and the policy is to maintain its secrecy.
contents.html_ja: NSA による審査が行われており、その秘密性を維持するというのが方針です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Q6. If this is true, why form an industry/government group to try to find commonly acceptable solutions?
contents.html_ja: Q6. それが事実なら、共通して受け入れられる解決策を探るために、なぜ産業界と政府の作業部会を設けるのか。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: It may be possible to use other encryption algorithms.
contents.html_ja: 他の暗号アルゴリズムを使えるかもしれません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: Q7. If the infrastructure in Tessera is already established and cannot be undone, then we may be wasting our time. Can we get more representation in the working industry/government working group from those who make the decisions?
contents.html_ja: Q7. Tessera の基盤がすでに確立されていて元に戻せないのなら、私たちは時間を無駄にしているのかもしれません。決定を下す人々に、産業界・政府の作業部会にもっと多く参加してもらうことはできませんか。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

contents.html: That can be arranged, perhaps not full time, but definitely for interim briefings.
contents.html_ja: それは手配できます。常時ではないかもしれませんが、少なくとも途中の説明のためには確実に参加できます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合した。

B.6 Stephen Walker and David Balenson: A Software Key Escrow Approach
B.7 Stephen Walker: A System for Software Integrity

As the U.S. builds its National Information Infrastructure (Nil), wide-spread use of encryption will be needed to protect sensitive information. However, wide-spread use of unconstrained encryption makes lawfully-authorized electronic surveillance difficult, if not impossible.

In attempting to balance the need for privacy and the need for lawful surveillance, a Key Escrow Encryption (KEE) technology was developed by the National Security Agency (NSA). The Escrowed Encryption Standard (EES) based on the KEE was issued by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Approved by the Secretary of Commerce^, this voluntary standard seeks to satisfy the need for privacy while preserving the ability to perform lawfully authorized wiretaps. This escrowed encryption technology is embodied in an electronic chip containing the SKIPJACK algorithm for encryption of information and the technology for creating a Law Enforcement Access Field (LEAF) for use in many telecommunication applications. Both the SKIPJACK algorithm and the LEAF creation method are classified. The standard is intended to facilitate the acquisition of devices that implement KEE technologies by Federal government agencies. Its use is not mandated for Federal agencies, the private sector, or other levels of government.

In using the Escrowed Encryption Standard, communications are encrypted by the SKIPJACK algorithm using a session key agreed upon by the participating entities. The appended LEAF field, which contains among other things the session key (encrypted using the device unique key), is itself encrypted with an 80-bit family key. The only known way of recovering the session key is to first recover the two 80-bit components of the device unique key. Each of these components is “escrowed” (i.e., filed) in encrypted form wdth one of two escrow agents. The two escrow agents act under strict procedures that wdU ensure security of the key components and govern their release. Surveillance requires acquisition of both escrowed key components, through a predefined process.

Based on the desire to use existing expertise in the private sector and motivated partially by require-ments of non-government entities, NIST has invited interested industry and academic partners to join a cooperative research consortium for developing the next generation of encryption technology that contains integrated cryptographic key escrowing techniques. In addition, an informal indus-try/government working group was established to explore the possibiUties of software implementation of key escrowing. Finally, representatives from key U.S. industries were invited to participate in this workshop in order to initiate a dialogue on the issues of escrowing encryption keys. This partnership with the private sector is necessary to arrive at a mutually acceptable solution that will balance the need for privacy, the need for lawful electronic surveillance, and the needs of industry, both as users and vendors. ^The following three quotations are from a February 4, 1994 a statement released by the White House Secretary: “Advanced encryption technology offers individuals cind businesses an inexpensive cuid eeisy way to encode data and telephone conversations. Unfortxmately, the same encryption technolo©^ that can help Americans protect business secrets and personal privacy can also be used by terrorists, drug dealers, aind other crimincds.” “... the Administration is announcing its intent to work with industry to develop other key escrow products that might better meet the needs of individuals and industry, particularly the American computer and telecommimications industry.” “The Administration is expanding its efforts to work with industry to improve on the Key Escrow chip, to develop key-escrow software, cind to examine alternatives to the Key Escrow chip.”
NIST Lecture Room B, Friday, June 10, 1994

8:45 Registration (Outside Lecture Room B) 9:00 Welcome: Raymond G. Kammer, Deputy Director, NIST 9:05 Workshop Overview and Participant Introductions: F. Lynn McNulty, CSL, NIST 9:15 Objectives of Key Escrow Encryption: Lionel S. “Skip” Johns, OSTP 9:40 NSA Perspectives: William P. Crowell, Deputy Director, NSA and Edward A. Hart, Deputy Director for Information Systems Security, NSA
10:00 Current “CLIPPER” Key Escrowing Method: Miles Smid, NIST 10:25 Industry Perspectives: (Position Papers, Participants)
Software Key Escrowing Proposal: Stephen Walker and David Balenson, Trusted Information Systems
Multi-Purpose Key Escrowing Methods: Silvio Micah, MIT Private Escrow Key Management: Jon Roberts, TECSEC Industry Responses, Suggestions: Participants
Criteria for High Integrity Software: Jim Arney, NSA System Requirements for Software Integrity: Stephen Walker, Trusted Information Systems Industry Suggestions: Participants
Dorothy Denning, Georgetown University Industry Suggestions: Participants
4:15 Summary/Future Directions: F. Lynn McNulty (Discussion) 4:45 Adjourn

Senior government officials discussed the objectives of the workshop in light of the key escrow encryption initiative announced in April, 1993. This initiative seeks to provide good encryption-based security to a number of information processing environments while preserving the lawful interests of law enforcement and national security. The Escrowed Encryption Standard (EES), announced as Federal Information Processing Standard 185 on February 4, 1994, resulted from this initiative. In addition, the “CLIPPER” escrowed encryption device was designed and built under this initiative. Finally, a Key Escrow System is being designed and implemented to store the escrowed keys securely and make them available to authorized entities for legally authorized electronic surveillance.

Raymond G. Kammer, Deputy Director of NIST, and F. Lynn McNulty, Associate Director for Computer Security at NIST, provided the welcoming and introductory remarks. (Mr. McNulty also served as moderator for the workshop.) Mssrs. Kammer and McNulty stated that the objective of the workshop was to engage the private sector in dialogue on the issues of key escrow encryption.

Lionel “Skip” Johns, Associate Director of Technology, Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President, stated that the National Security Council has the responsibility of coordinating security policy in the Executive Branch of the U.S. Government. Intelhgence remains a critical activity of national interest and the U.S. must be able to detect and act in a timely manner on real threats of terrorism, crime, and- danger to the national security. OSTP seeks to engage in dialogue with U.S. industry so that effective intelhgence collection can be conducted with a minimal threat to privacy. He stated that acceptable solutions may be hard to find and, unfortunately, a final solution may be suboptimal.

William Crowell, Deputy Director of the National Security Agency, pointed out the need to ensure that a balance is achieved among four equities: privacy, public safety, ability to market new prod-ucts, and national security. Three options, when implementing cryptography, are possible: flawed cryptography, strong cryptography with contents unreadable by all, and key escrowing. The lat-ter seemed to have the most viability for achieving balance among the four equities. CLIPPER is a first (interim) solution - there is a need to look at more software intensive solutions. Edward Hart, Deputy Director for Information Systems Security, NSA, reiterated NSA’s desire for openness, coUegiality, and desire to work with U.S. industry in seeking mutually acceptable solutions.
Industry participants, in an open discussion, raised the following issues/questions/concerns:
Currently the delay in obtaining licenses to export products prevents U.S. industry from being internationally competitive.

The uncertainty over whether a Ucense will be granted discourages even applying for a hcense. There needs to be more information as to what apphcations have been made and their dispo-sition. A counter-point is the need for nondisclosure of export license apphcations that might compromise the economic interests of the apphcants or compromise the interests of national security.
Given the four equities, how are we planning for change? It is important that we not be constrained in meeting future needs.

2.2 Session 2: Current Key Escrow Encryption Method This session summarized the current key escrowing system designed to work with EES devices such as CLIPPER. Industry representatives were given the opportunity to present their positions.
2.2.1 Current “CLIPPER Chip Key Escrowing System”, Miles Smid, Key Escrow

Intensive work on the key escrowing system began with the April 16, 1993 announcement of the KEE Initiative. NIST appointed a program manager in August. In addition to NIST, other participating agencies are the Department of Justice, the FBI, the Department of Treasury, and the NSA.

View graphs were shown describing how the KEE system is designed to work: manufacturing of the chip, programming of the the chip, key escrowing with two independent government agents (NIST, Department of Treasury) obtaining court authorization for a wire tap and the corresponding release
, of keys, and decryption of communications.

Four phases of key escrowing have been defined. The first phase, consisting of developing a pro-totype system, has been completed. The first programming of a chip took place in October, 1993 and by March, 1994, the keys for 17,000 CLIPPER chips had been escrowed. At present, no key components have been released. Phases 2-4 are designed to move from the prototype system to a target production system. The target system will include automated procedures for handling and storing escrow components, a decryption processor, a simple key component extraction system, an escrow agent workstation, and a transition to life cycle support. A number of evaluations are planned during phases 2-4. Recent efforts have included preparing for key escrowing for CAPSTONE. Also, the Vice-President has asked for a review of other possible escrow agents.

2.3 Session 3: Key Escrow Encryption Alternative #1 Session Coordinator: Don Cole, Chief Scientist, Racal-Guardata, Inc.

NIST has pubhshed announcements seeking Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (CRADAs) with organizations having the capability and interest in developing alternative key escrow encryption methods, especially in software but also in hardware. As a result, several organizations are participating in a Key Escrow Encryption Working Group seeking to specify requirements and acceptability criteria for key escrow encryption systems and then to design and/or evaluate candidate systems.

2.3.1 A Software Key Escrow Approach, Stephen T. Walker (Member of Working Group) and David M. Balenson, Trusted Information Systems, Inc. A working group consisting of four non-government individuals (Cole, Denning, Upton, Walker) and two government agency individuals (Arney, Branstad) have been exploring ways to perform key es-crow encryption in software. The motivation is to develop a broadly acceptable, low-cost system that achieves the objectives of law enforcement. It does not solve problems that CLIPPER/CAPSTONE do not solve as both can be defeated by a determined software hacker.

Many aspects of the design and usage are similar to the specifications in the EES. Rather than secret key cryptography, the proposed model uses pubhc key cryptography and will work with any pubhc key algorithm although software implementations cannot keep the algorithm secret. It will work

with cards. Components of a private key are escrowed with two independent escrow agents. Each instance of the software is a shrink-wrapped package, with a unique ED assigned to it either at the time of creation or the time of first invocation, and with embedded cryptographic checksums to guard against code modification. This ED is provided in a LEAF which is created by the software when invoked. The method of escrowing keys and their authorized retrieval by law enforcement agencies was outlined.
TIS is currently building a working prototype. They are also looking at some alternatives that do not parallel the aspects of CLIPPER/CAPSTONE.
2.4 Session 4: Key Escrow Encryption Alternatives #2 Session Coordinator: Jimmy Upton, President, Uptronics

Individuals may desire key escrowing as a backup procedure in case the normal key management system malfunctions or their valuable information cannot be decrypted because the key is lost. Corporations may desire key escrowing to prevent employees from holding encrypted information “hostage” Representatives from academia and industry presented approaches to key escrowing for
corporate purposes and for multiple purposes.
2.4.1 Multi-Purpose Key Escrowing Methods, Silvio Micaii, Massachusetts Institute

Key escrowing is fundamentally a good idea, but something more is required. The need for key escrowing may arise in multiple contexts: state vs. company (may need keys escrowed inside), communications vs. stored data (will be retrieved later), simple private call (friend) vs. recorded private call (stock broker), national vs. international context, etc. What is needed is multi-purpose key escrowing.

The proposal is for “Fair PubHc Key Cryptography (PKC)” as an alternative to the CLIPPER Chip. Fair PKC is distributed, flexible, open, economical, and complete, whereas the CLIPPER Chip is centralized, rigid, hidden, expensive, and partial. Private key cryptosystems have limited use because of the need for key management; on the other hand, in public key cryptosystems, through the use of public directories, it is easy to talk to someone you have never met. In the CLIPPER chip, the focus of attention has been on the issues of escrowing, but communicating entities still need to estabhsh a session key.

From a law enforcement perspective, the idea of combining pubHc key cryptosystems with private key cryptosystems is not a good one. Individuals can use the public system to exchange the private key K and then can use a standard method (e.g., DES) to encrypt. The key is not available to law enforcement for an authorized wiretap. Furthermore, the encryption can be made reasonably strong, e.g., EKADK2{EKx{rnessage))). Fair PKC works in the following way. First, determine a public key PRT, secret key SK pair. The secret key is divided into two components SKi and SK2, the first of which is escrowed with trustee Ti and the second escrowed with T2- Each of Ti and T2 can certify that they have a legitimate component of SK without actually knowing the other component. The pubhc key is filed with a center and approved (i.e., made available for distribution). Law enforcement requires acquisition of the secret key components from the trustees. Here is an analogy of how Fair PKC might work. Suppose the public key is X and the private key is y/X^ where the square root is performed modulo some number n. The difficulty of flnding the secret key is based on the difficulty of flnding the square root (which is as hard as factoring). The user selects two numbers which are defined to be y/a and y/b and serve as SKi and SK2. The user forms a = (-y/a)^ and b = (\/6)^,the pubhc key X = a*b, and the secret key y/X = y/a*y/b. Trustee Ti is given {X, a, 6 y/a) and T2 is given (X, a, 6 y/b) where a is less b. Ti can check X = a* and =

a and similarly T2 can certify that it has a component of a legitimate secret key. But each is unable to determine the component held by the other trustee. A law enforcement agency, if authorized, can obtain the components from the trustees and form the private key ^/X.
An important fact is that there is more than one (modulo n) factorization of X = a*b, so the key cam be escrowed in different ways with different trustees.
In comparing the CLIPPER chip approach to Fair PKC, one finds:
Control: With CLIPPER, the user does not choose the encryption algorithm. With Fair PKC, the user chooses both the algorithm and the keys.
Cost: CLIPPER requires secure hardware. Fair PKC allows either hardware or software.
Prior Exchanges: In using the CLIPPER chip, a prior exchange of the session key is necessary. In Fair PKC, no prior exchanges are required.
Compatibility: Using CLIPPER, there are only two trustees. In Fair PKC, many independent sets of trustees are possible.
International Isolation: With CLIPPER, yes - with Fair PKC, no.
Ambiguity: With CLIPPER, yes - with Fair PKC, no.
Reliabihty: In CLIPPER, if a single trustee goes down, the court-authorized wire-tapping is not possible. In Fair PKC, “n of m” trustees is enough, e.g. 3 of 5.
Duration of Tap: With CLIPPER, a tap can be forever. With Fair PKC, a tap is only for a court-authorized period of time.
The right key escrow system should be flexible, interoperable, economical, simple, and multi-purpose.

Session Coordinator: James F. Dray, Advanced Authentication Initiative Leader, NIST

Use of a key escrowed encryption device in a security application requires a high level of system integrity to assure that all security relevant events are performed correctly. Utilization of a key escrowed encryption device (e.g. CAPSTONE) in a more complex information processing appHcation such as distributed electronic commerce requires many functions of the computer system to have high integrity, both to assure that the data is properly protected and also that the the LEAF field is transmitted and received properly. Integrity requirements for software encryption and operating system controlled execution were the subject of this session.

Jim Dray presented a model for an escrowed encryption device. Important points to be noted are the need for an interface between the cryptographic device and the general purpose system and the need to communicate through untrusted layers of software. The threat scenaxios include all communication pairs: rogue system/rogue system, rogue system/legitimate system, legitimate system/legitimate system. The high-level implications are that one needs to prevent use of an EES device that circumvents the LEAF; it would be ideal to design cryptographic modules to withstand attacks in an untrusted environment; and the LEAF imposes additional requirements.
2.5.1 Criteria for High Integrity Software Encryption, .Tames W. Arney, Chief, De-

A system security paradigm was outlined for evaluating KEE alternatives. It is important to remind oneself about the user/customer needs for integrity, confidentiality, and availability. Design require-ments are needed to approach the problem. The development of a solution is evolutionary because initial perspectives may be short-sighted and because threats may change. Evaluation/verification is required. The design requirements need to consider both the higher algorithm/protocol level and also the implementation level in hardware and software. Good software engineering is a starting point to the effective protection of embedded software cryptography.
2.5.2 System Requirements for Softwzure Integrity, Stephen W. Walker, President,

Software integrity is needed unless the entire computing system is packaged in a box that is highly resistant to reverse engineering. Two years ago, TIS was asked by ARPA to develop technical means for controlling high-performance workstations so that the government might be willing to allow their export to such countries as China and Russia for use in “approved” applications. In this project (called the ARPA Safeguards Project), a technology base was identified for controlling the execution of the operating system so that it would only run on a given machine; its modification would be resisted by storing it on some kind of read-only medium; and it would be packaged in a tamper-resistant box (which included methods of tamper detection and audit reporting to the U.S.).

The insight gained in developing these controlled execution procedures is directly applicable to any software system where the integrity of the software must be preserved. It can be used for controlled
execution of an operating system. The programs are stored on and require a digital signature as authorization to effect an update (therefore also resistant to viruses).

The analysis performed in this project has shown that these same techniques can be used in software-only deployments of encryption and key escrow. The approach will not allow the use of classified algorithms in software since there is no way to protect them from disclosure.

2.5.3 Industry Suggestions, Participants Jim Schindler and Keith Klemba described the work of Hewlett-Packard Company. HP had looked at its domestic/foreign customer base to determine what was needed. The sentiments were that security functions were needed in both hardware and software; there was a need to stabilize the manner in which the crypto technology interfaces with applications; and a common cryptographic policy framework was needed for various governments.

HP has designed a “national fiag” card (NFC), about the size of a postage stamp, that would enforce the cryptographic policy of a nation. The NFC would fit into a drawer in a cryptographic unit (CU) which is designed to provide cryptographic services (under the strict control of the NFC). The NFC is removable, interchangeable, and expirable. The CU would be designed for performance and protection with customization for a given host system. The initial discussions for the CU have centered around a PCMCIA haxdwaxe format. The CU features protection of the keys and algorithms and would Ukely have to be certified.

The host system is some hardware component that delivers information technology service to the user (e.g., personal computer or laptop, workstation, network server, mainframe, network printer, personal digital assistant). Gateways would be required to allow for two nationality systems to interconnect. There would be free export of the host system, and national security fears would be eased because governments can play a role.
HP wants to sell equipment everywhere and needs the cryptography issue problem to be solved.

2.6 Session 6: International Key Escrow Encryption - Proposed Objec-

Dorothy Denning talked about her personal research on international aspects of key escrowing. Four general requirements were identified for an international key escrow system: encryption products that provide secure communications, a key escrow system for authorized government access, international communications, and use of encryption products outside of the country that holds the key.

The general properties of escrowed encryption are: strong security, authorized government access, hardware or software implementations, classified or unclassified algorithms, multiple standards and gateways, and private sector key escrow - separate or integrated.

National control is needed over the import/export/use of products and over who holds the keys. International and bilateral agreements are needed to assist in criminal investigations, sharing of technologies, and constraints on the sale and use of products. Several national policy options for export and for internal use of products were presented. Law enforcement scenarios were enumerated, e.g., country A wishes to investigate subject X from country B and country C holds the encryption key.

Government to create a key escrowing task force, run by NIST under policy guidance of the NSC/OSTP-led Interagency Working Group to manage and expedite the search for key escrow alternatives.
